headline: LLM Inference in a Flash reports compressed KV caching and modeled Compute-in-Flash gains
summary: The paper combines integer-only compute-in-flash inference with a static flash-resident dictionary that stores compressed KV-cache codes. On LongBench, the authors report that the combined pipeline retains 99% of the FP16 full-KV baseline score across Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B, with less than one average score-point degradation and nearly 15× dynamic KV traffic compression. Separately, an analytical model for Llama-3.1-8B at batch size 1 projects 3.1× lower decode latency and 2.7× lower energy at 1K context, and 4.4×/6.8× at 256K, against an NPU+DDR5 full-KV baseline. These system-level numbers are modeled, not measurements on physical Compute-in-Flash hardware; prefill is outside the study.
